messages:
marie: Heads up — us-west1 GPU pool spiking with nodes transitioning to NotReady/NoSchedule after yesterday's kernel patch. Device plugin logs show duplicated device entries and pci bus reset flapping. Autoscaler is not adding replacement capacity because taints are sticky. :eyes:

alex: Seeing same. quick logs: ```Aug 12 03:22:11 node-gtx-03 kernel: NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus. Aug 12 03:22:12 node-gtx-03 nvidia-device-plugin: failed to register device /dev/nvidia0: file exists``` kubelet marks node Ready->NotReady with NoSchedule taint.

vikram: Can someone paste `kubectl describe node node-gtx-03`? wondering if kubelet is evicting pods or kube-proxy is choking on missing device.

marie: ```Name: node-gtx-03 Conditions: Ready False (kernel: pci reset) Taints: nvidia.com/gpu=unavailable:NoSchedule Allocatable: nvidia.com/gpu: 0 Capacity: nvidia.com/gpu: 1 Non-terminated Pods: 12``` Pods with GPU requests are stuck in Pending.

jen: Autoscaler shows scale-up blocked: "No capacity: insufficient nodes matching required taints/labels". It doesn't replace because the tainted nodes are still considered part of pool and pod can't schedule to new spot nodes due to GPU label mismatch.

alex: Quick workaround: cordon & drain the affected nodes, restart kubelet and nvidia-device-plugin daemonset on them. Doing rolling restart now on 3 nodes. Commands: ```kubectl cordon node-gtx-03 && kubectl drain node-gtx-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data && kubectl rollout restart daemonset nvidia-device-plugin -n kube-system```

nvidia-monitor-bot: Alert: 6 nodes with 'GPU has fallen off the bus' in the last 30m in us-west1. Average recovery time 18m.

vikram: After restart we still see duplicated /dev entries on one host. `ls -l /dev | grep nvidia` shows `/dev/nvidia0` and `/dev/nvidia0_old` created by udev race. Need to check udev rules and driver init ordering vs device-plugin.

marie: Files from node: ```# journalctl -u nvidia-driver -n 50 --no-pager Aug 12 03:21:59 node-gtx-03 systemd[1]: Starting NVIDIA driver setup... Aug 12 03:22:10 node-gtx-03 nvidia-driver[2345]: modprobe: ERROR: could not insert 'nvidia': Unknown symbol in module``` Looks like kernel module mismatch with new kernel image on some hosts (kernel-5.19 vs driver compiled for 5.15).

alex: That's important — some node images were updated and didn't rebuild driver kernel module. Risky mix of rolling kernel upgrades across the pool. We should pin node-image version for GPU pools until driver rebuilds are validated.

jen: Ops question: do we have capacity in on-demand pool to shift traffic? Preemptible (spot) GPU pool is most of capacity. If we move some workloads to on-demand it will cost more but reduce recovery churn. Cost hit estimate: +$7k/day if we shift 50% of production GPU traffic to on-demand.

vikram: For immediate mitigation: 1) cordon affected nodes, 2) trigger node-image rollback for hosts on kernel-5.19, 3) trigger a rebuild/deployment of the nvidia kernel module package in our image pipeline, 4) set autoscaler to ignore taints for a short window so replacement nodes come up. I'll open a PR for the autoscaler temp policy change.

marie: I'm doing the rollback for 4 hosts now. Also adding a preflight check in the node boot script to verify nvidia-smi responds before marking ready. Suggest we also add a liveness probe for the device-plugin that restarts container on duplicate-device errors.

deploy-bot: Started job #3821: node-image-rollback -> us-west1-gpu-pool. Job link: https://ci.internal/jobs/3821

alex: Follow-up: create a short runbook for oncall: how to recognize pci-reset vs driver-abi mismatch, commands to drain/unstick autoscaler, and cost tradeoffs for shifting to on-demand. I'll draft and post to #help.

marie: Filing incident ticket and RCA owner. Summary: kernel/driver mismatch + udev/device-plugin race produced duplicate /dev nodes -> kubelet marks GPU allocatable zero -> nodes tainted NoSchedule -> autoscaler didn't replace due to taint/label mismatch -> capacity gap.

jen: Thanks all. Keep updates here. If any node doesn't recover after rollback+restart, we'll escalate to vendor support (NVIDIA + cloud). :shipit:
